export const meta = {
  name: 'viewer-ux-slices',
  description: 'Implement one step of the viewer UX PRD: each slice in its own worktree, then an independent review and a fix pass',
  whenToUse: 'Run with args {step, slices:[{key,title,worktree,branch,brief,others}]} for one step of docs/PRD_VIEWER_UX.md section 11',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Implement', detail: 'red/green TDD per slice in its own worktree' },
    { title: 'Review', detail: 'independent adversarial review of each slice diff against the PRD' },
    { title: 'Fix', detail: 'close confirmed review findings' },
  ],
}

const SCRATCH = '/tmp/claude-1000/-home-agentops-dev-md-manager/541817b2-200f-49c5-b924-e4e11cf0112a/scratchpad/ux'
const common = (s) => `
You are implementing slice ${s.key.toUpperCase()} ("${s.title}") of docs/PRD_VIEWER_UX.md in the MD Manager repo.

WORKTREE: ${s.worktree} (git branch ${s.branch}, created from feature/viewer-ux). Work ONLY in this directory. node_modules is a symlink to the shared install; never run npm install.
NEVER touch: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager (the user's live checkout), any other worktree, the dev servers on ports 3001/5173, ~/.config/md-manager, ~/.local/state. Do not push.

READ FIRST in the PRD (docs/PRD_VIEWER_UX.md in your worktree): sections 2 (goals + confirmed decisions), 3, the ${s.key.toUpperCase()} row and the parallel-safety rules of section 11, every section your slice implements (4.x, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10 as relevant), and section 12 (your unit tests, your browser scenarios in 12.2, your migrations in 12.3). The PRD is the source of truth; where the code contradicts a PRD claim, trust the code, make the smallest sensible choice, and report it as a deviation.
Real captured payloads for fixtures and sanity checks: ${SCRATCH}/api/*.json (skeleton-001 failed at review, skeleton-fixes-001 succeeded, workflow-guardrails-001 two lanes). Screenshots of the current UI: ${SCRATCH}/shots/.

SLICE BRIEF: ${s.brief}

PARALLEL SAFETY: another slice may be running at the same time in another worktree. ${s.others} Do not edit files outside your slice's file list in section 11 unless unavoidable; list any such file in your report.

METHOD (the repo's PRD/TDD rules):
1. Write your slice's new unit tests and browser scenarios FIRST (per 12.1/12.2), run them against the unchanged code and record the failing output. The red must be behavioural (an assertion failing for the reason in the PRD table), not a compile/import error: add a skeleton export when needed. Record test-authoring mistakes separately from product reds.
2. Implement. Keep the code idiomatic for this repo (read neighbouring files; match their comment density, naming, CSS conventions, testids, accessibility patterns).
3. Green: run ONLY targeted checks — your unit tests (npx tsx --test <files>), \`npx tsc -b\`, \`npx eslint <changed files>\`, and Playwright for your new spec plus every existing spec you migrated or whose components you changed, in BOTH phases:
   \`npx playwright test -c tests/project-workflows/playwright.config.ts <spec files> --reporter=line\` (worker phase, mocks) and the same with \`WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=candidate\` (seeded real API). Run one Playwright invocation at a time. Do NOT run the full suites; the orchestrator does that after merging.
   If you change src/App.tsx or anything outside src/projects, also run the root skills specs that could be affected with free ports: \`MD_MANAGER_WEB_PORT=5184 MD_MANAGER_API_PORT=3014 npx playwright test <spec> --reporter=line\` (never ports 5173/3001).
4. Write docs/handoff/ux-${s.key}.md: what shipped, red evidence (command + key failing lines), green evidence, migrations with one-line reasons, deviations from the PRD, follow-ups.
5. Commit on ${s.branch} (one or a few commits). Messages like "Viewer UX ${s.key.toUpperCase()}: <what>" in the repo's style (imperative subject, body explaining why), ending with the line:
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Leave the worktree clean (git status empty apart from ignored files).`

const IMPL_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    summary: { type: 'string' },
    commits: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    files_outside_slice: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    red_evidence: { type: 'string' },
    green_evidence: { type: 'string' },
    deviations: { type: 'string' },
    open_issues: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['summary', 'commits', 'files_outside_slice', 'red_evidence', 'green_evidence', 'deviations', 'open_issues'],
}
const REVIEW_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    findings: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['P0', 'P1', 'P2', 'P3'] },
      file: { type: 'string' }, line: { type: 'integer' },
      summary: { type: 'string' },
      failure_scenario: { type: 'string' },
      confirmed: { type: 'boolean' },
    }, required: ['severity', 'file', 'summary', 'failure_scenario', 'confirmed'] } },
    spec_gaps: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'things the slice row / its scenarios / its migrations require that are missing' },
    notes: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['findings', 'spec_gaps', 'notes'],
}
const FIX_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    outcomes: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      item: { type: 'string' }, outcome: { type: 'string', enum: ['fixed', 'not_a_defect', 'deferred'] }, note: { type: 'string' },
    }, required: ['item', 'outcome', 'note'] } },
    commits: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    green_evidence: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['outcomes', 'commits', 'green_evidence'],
}

const results = await pipeline(
  args.slices,
  s => agent(`${common(s)}\n\nImplement the slice now.`, { label: `implement:${s.key}`, phase: 'Implement', schema: IMPL_SCHEMA }),
  (impl, s) => impl && agent(`You are an independent reviewer of slice ${s.key.toUpperCase()} ("${s.title}") of docs/PRD_VIEWER_UX.md.
Worktree ${s.worktree}, branch ${s.branch}; review \`git -C ${s.worktree} diff feature/viewer-ux..${s.branch}\` and the files it touches. READ-ONLY: do not edit or commit; you may run targeted tests (npx tsx --test, npx tsc -b, eslint, and at most one Playwright spec run at a time with -c tests/project-workflows/playwright.config.ts). Never touch /home/agentops/dev/md-manager or ports 3001/5173.
The implementer reported:\n${JSON.stringify(impl, null, 1)}
Check, adversarially:
1. Correctness bugs in the new code (edge cases from the real payloads in ${SCRATCH}/api/: null node_id events, print reviews without events, attempts, lanes, time zones, polling, empty states).
2. Conformance to the slice row in section 11, the relevant design sections, its 12.2 scenarios and 12.3 migrations: list what is missing as spec_gaps.
3. Tests that cannot fail or do not test the claim (look at each new assertion); red evidence that was only a compile error.
4. Regressions: behaviour the existing suites rely on (testids, honesty wording substrings pinned in section 8, expectNoExecutionControls, accessibility: roles, keyboard, focus), read-only guarantee, mobile overflow.
5. Code quality relative to the surrounding code (dead code, duplication, needless complexity).
Report only real defects with a concrete failure scenario; mark confirmed only if you reproduced it or traced it with certainty.`,
    { label: `review:${s.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: REVIEW_SCHEMA }).then(review => ({ impl, review })),
  (prev, s) => {
    if (!prev || !prev.review) return prev
    const todo = [
      ...prev.review.findings.filter(f => f.severity !== 'P3' || f.confirmed),
      ...prev.review.spec_gaps.map(g => ({ severity: 'gap', summary: g })),
    ]
    if (!todo.length) return { ...prev, fix: null }
    return agent(`${common(s)}\n\nThe slice is implemented and committed on ${s.branch}. An independent review found the items below. Fix every real one (verify each first; a reviewer can be wrong — then mark not_a_defect with the reason). Defer only what genuinely belongs to a later slice per section 11, saying which. Re-run the targeted checks for what you touched (both Playwright phases for affected specs), update docs/handoff/ux-${s.key}.md, commit, leave the worktree clean.\n\nITEMS:\n${JSON.stringify(todo, null, 1)}`,
      { label: `fix:${s.key}`, phase: 'Fix', schema: FIX_SCHEMA }).then(fix => ({ ...prev, fix }))
  },
)
return results.map((r, i) => ({ slice: args.slices[i].key, ...r }))

slices.title: Time, freshness, trim (client and test plumbing)
slices.brief: Section 11 row S1: time.ts (formatClock/formatAgo/formatSpan/spanBetween), Time.tsx (<time dateTime title>), useNow, TimeZoneToggle (time-zone-toggle, localStorage mdm.projects.timezone with try/catch), LiveStatus (live-status with data-state live/watching/stale/finished/hidden) beside the status badge on today's run title row; useResource meta {settledAt,lastError,failures}; ProjectsView passes the run resource's meta to RunView; header Refresh becomes a background reload (refreshToken moves into token) without blanking, plus the Projects Refresh busy state; durations on check rows and reviewers; the two footnotes removed (RunView status enum footnote, NodeDetail node footnote); the overflow-wrap fix; tests/project-workflows/playwright.config.ts timezoneId 'UTC' and locale 'en-GB'; package.json test:unit glob (keep the existing server/*.test.ts files listed as they are, add tests/unit/*.test.ts); the fixture extension point (tests/project-workflows/fixtures/index.ts aggregator + seven empty fixtures/ux-*.ts modules wired into fixtures.ts maps and seedCandidate, per the section 11 rules); new tests/project-workflows/ux-time.spec.ts (time-local-utc, live-freshness) and tests/unit/time.test.ts; the S1 migrations in 12.3 (inputs.spec.ts receipt times and worker-stop, guardrails.spec.ts shown() helper and its uses). Replace formatTime call sites (~20) with <Time>. Keep status.ts formatTime removal consistent (no dangling imports). The live chip for a succeeded/cancelled run says finished and polling stops (already the case in ProjectsView).
slices.others: Slice S2 runs concurrently and owns contracts/projects/triage.ts, tests/unit/triage.test.ts and tests/unit/fixtures/runs/*; do not create or edit those.

slices.title: Model (pure triage module)
slices.brief: Section 11 row S2: new contracts/projects/triage.ts (pure TypeScript, no React, importable by both the client and the server) exporting buildTimeline (5.1/5.2 rules 1-11), deriveNow (6.2: the situation table with the scope rule, focus node, reason sources 0-4, the rule 5 cases a-d, the command forms of 6.1 as structured data: label, RUNBOOK section, numbered steps of {kind:'command',text}|{kind:'text',text}, never concrete invented names), deriveFocus, deriveAttention, humanizeEvent (5.3 humanized messages), gateReasonsByCheck (4.6, including the unkeyed <path> command-tail rule), attemptResultUris, laneLines; memoization per 5.1. Plus tests/unit/triage.test.ts covering every case in 12.1 (one test per deriveNow situation named by its data-situation) using trimmed JSON fixtures in tests/unit/fixtures/runs/ made from the captured payloads (trim to what the tests need; redact nothing new — the payloads are already redacted) and synthetic runs. Verify every command string against the real CLI: workflow/pipeline.py argparse, workflow/guardrails.py (answer, resume --accept-challenge), workflow/repair.py (repair --workspace/--commit/--reason/--dry-run), workflow/scaffold.py (init), workflow/launch.py (launch --repo --run-id --live --automatic), workflow/interactive.py (attach-one --node), and RUNBOOK.md section names. Types for inputs come from contracts/projects/v1.ts (RunDetail, WorkflowEvent, RunInputs, ReviewResult, WorkerResult); do not change v1.ts. Run your tests with `npx tsx --test tests/unit/triage.test.ts` (S1 adds the glob later). Design the API so S3 (run page: NowBanner, CommandBlock, StepsTimeline, StepStrip) and S5 (server activity field) can consume it directly; document it with brief doc comments.
slices.others: Slice S1 runs concurrently and owns package.json and everything under src/ and tests/project-workflows/; do not edit those. You own only contracts/projects/triage.ts, tests/unit/triage.test.ts, tests/unit/fixtures/runs/*, and docs/handoff/ux-s2.md.

impl.summary:
S1 is done on branch ux/s1 in /home/agentops/dev/mdm-ux-s1, in two commits. The worktree is clean apart from ignored node_modules and test-results; nothing was pushed. All targeted checks pass in both phases.

What changed:
- **Time display.**
  - Every run, node, check, event, receipt, question, reviewer and challenge time is now a `<time dateTime title>` element. It shows local time by default, with the full UTC time in the tooltip. The date appears only when it differs from the run's start day, or from today in lists.
  - A Local/UTC toggle (`time-zone-toggle`) sits beside the run status. The choice is remembered in localStorage key `mdm.projects.timezone`, wrapped in try/catch.
  - All 18 `formatTime` call sites were replaced, and `formatTime` was removed from status.ts.
  - New files: `src/projects/time.ts`, `Time.tsx`, `useNow.ts`, `TimeZoneToggle.tsx`.
- **Live chip.** `src/projects/LiveStatus.tsx` renders `live-status` with `data-state` live, watching, stale, finished or hidden. Stale means two failed polls in a row or 15 s without a success, and it is announced once. It reads the new `useResource` meta { settledAt, lastError, failures, refreshing }, which ProjectsView passes to RunView.
- **Refresh.** Refresh now reloads in the background (the refresh token moved into the request token), so the page no longer blanks and keeps its scroll position and tab. The Projects Refresh button is disabled, `aria-busy` and reads "Refreshing…" until every shown level has settled.
- **Durations and trim.**
  - Check rows show durations (`.check-duration`), and reviewers show "took 3m49s" (`.reviewer-duration`).
  - Both status footnotes are removed; each status badge now carries a short `title` (`STATUS_TITLE`).
  - `overflow-wrap: anywhere` is set on `.node-detail` and `.worker-summary`.
- **Test plumbing.**
  - Playwright config pins `timezoneId` UTC and `locale` en-GB.
  - `test:unit` keeps the six server test files and adds `tests/unit/*.test.ts`.
  - New tests: `tests/unit/time.test.ts` (16 tests) and `tests/project-workflows/ux-time.spec.ts` (scenarios time-local-utc and live-freshness).
  - The S1 migrations are applied in inputs.spec.ts and guardrails.spec.ts.
- **Fixture extension point.**
  - `tests/project-workflows/fixtures/index.ts` aggregates seven empty modules (ux-time, ux-run, ux-node, ux-verify, ux-launch, ux-review, ux-lists).
  - It merges their payloads into the maps fixtures.ts exports; mock.ts loads it with a side-effect import.
  - `seedCandidate` passes each module a SeedContext. A module's seed returns its workflows and optional top-level registry keys, which S6 needs for `viewer.expose_run_dir`.
  - fixtures.ts now exports the builders later modules need.
  - A temporary probe module (not committed) confirmed the wiring works in both phases.

The handoff is at /home/agentops/dev/mdm-ux-s1/docs/handoff/ux-s1.md.
commits: eea0fb3 Viewer UX S1: fixture extension point for the UX slices
f5d6ef6 Viewer UX S1: local/UTC times, live chip and background Refresh
files_outside_slice: tests/project-workflows/mock.ts (one side-effect import of fixtures/index.ts; fixtures.ts cannot import the aggregator without an import cycle)
src/projects/panels.tsx (StatusBadge gets a title, the replacement section 8 prescribes for the removed footnotes)
impl.red_evidence:
Unit, against a skeleton time.ts: `npx tsx --test tests/unit/time.test.ts` gave 16 tests, 15 failed, 1 passed. The one pass is the "unreadable value shown as served" case, which the skeleton passes trivially. Typical failures:
- `actual: '' expected: '0s'`
- `actual: '2026-03-01T10:20:00Z' expected: '10:20'`
- `actual: 'live' expected: 'watching'`

Browser, worker phase: `npx playwright test -c tests/project-workflows/playwright.config.ts ux-time.spec.ts inputs.spec.ts guardrails.spec.ts --reporter=line` gave 4 failed, 9 passed:
- time-local-utc: `toHaveText("02:00")`, element not found (no `<time>` elements).
- live-freshness: `toHaveAttribute("data-state","finished")`, element not found (no `live-status`).
- inputs worker-inputs: `time[datetime="2026-03-01T10:00:00Z"]` not found.
- guardrails worker-questions-shown: `time[title="2026-03-01 10:07:00 UTC"]` not found.

A temporary copy holding only the Refresh part of live-freshness showed Refresh blanking the page: `expect(getByText('Loading run run-failed')).toHaveCount(0)` gave Expected 0, Received 1.

Candidate phase (`WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=candidate`): the same 4 failed, 9 passed.

Test-authoring mistakes, kept separate from the product reds:
- `window` used inside `page.evaluate` callbacks, which `tsc` rejects because tests compile without the DOM lib.
- `refresh.click()` scrolled the header button into view and reset the measured scroll position. Now `dispatchEvent('click')`.
- The scroll position was read before the node page settled. The spec now waits for `checks-list` and `node-events`, then polls until scrollY is 400.
impl.green_evidence:
- `npx tsx --test tests/unit/time.test.ts`: 16 passed.
- `npx tsc -b`: clean.
- `npx eslint` on every changed or new .ts/.tsx file: clean.
- Worker phase, all 8 project-workflows spec files (S1 changed components every one of them renders): `npx playwright test -c tests/project-workflows/playwright.config.ts --reporter=line` gave 36 passed (3.1m).
- Candidate phase, same command with `WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=candidate`: 36 passed (3.3m). After a hover-only CSS change, ux-time, inputs and guardrails were re-run on the final tree: 13 passed.
- Root skills specs for the App.tsx header change: `MD_MANAGER_WEB_PORT=5184 MD_MANAGER_API_PORT=3014 npx playwright test tests/graph.spec.ts tests/listing-refresh.spec.ts` gave 16 passed.
- Extension-point probe (temporary, reverted): 1 passed in each phase.
- The new glob expands to document, editSession, model and time unit tests.

The first full worker run failed 2 tests. Both were fixed before the runs above: one was the scroll test-authoring mistake, the other was `lanes.spec.ts:102` (deviation 1).
impl.deviations:
1. **Stop line wording.** It reads "Stop confirmed at 10:20." rather than the PRD's "Stopped 10:20 · stop confirmed" (12.3). `lanes.spec.ts:102` pins the substring "Stop confirmed", 12.3 does not list it, and section 8 keeps pinned substrings. The inputs.spec.ts:155 migration asserts the new text. S4b must migrate `lanes.spec.ts:102` when it rewrites the stop line.
2. **"A check row shows 3s".** No fixture has a 3 s check, and the PRD lists no S1 fixture. The scenario asserts 1m00s and 5m00s on `run-succeeded/verify_ui` instead, and the unit test covers the 2.54 s → "3s" rounding. `ux-time.ts` stays empty.
3. **mock.ts edited.** It gets one side-effect import. The aggregator mutates the maps fixtures.ts exports rather than fixtures.ts importing the aggregator, because a cycle through the modules would break depending on which file a spec imports first.
4. **panels.tsx edited.** StatusBadge gets a `title` from `STATUS_TITLE`, per section 8's replacement for the removed footnotes.
5. **Extension-point extras.**
   - fixtures.ts exports its builders, and `projectReview` takes an optional `workflowId`.
   - seed.ts exports `SeedContext`, `RunOptions` and `InternalEvent`.
   - A module's seed returns `{workflows, registry?}` so S6 can add `viewer.expose_run_dir`.
6. **Time reference provider.** `TimeReferenceContext` is provided where ProjectsView renders RunView rather than inside RunView. The scope is the same, and it avoids re-indenting RunView.
7. **Chip placement.** The chip and toggle sit in `.run-status-row` beside the `run-status` line, under the h2, because the status badge lives in `run-status` and not on the h2 row.
8. **Extra meta field.** `ResourceMeta` has a fourth field, `refreshing`, which drives the Refresh busy state.
9. **Assignment.tsx unchanged.** It has no `formatTime` call site.
10. **No policy.json.** There is no `features/viewer-ux-s1/policy.json`, because S1 ships as a direct commit. The scenario ids are time-local-utc and live-freshness.
impl.open_issues:
- **S3.** Move `LiveStatus` and `TimeZoneToggle` into RunHeader with the same testids, then drop `.run-status-row` and `.run-freshness` from App.css. time-local-utc expects `run-status` to stay on the toggle's row, and the created time to stay a `<time>` on the run page.
- **S4b.** Migrate `lanes.spec.ts:102` if the stop wording changes. PRD 12.3 should also list that line.
- **S6.** Adds the controller suffix to LiveStatus.
- **Pressed-button hover.** The app-wide `.button:hover` rule outranks `.button[aria-pressed='true']`, so any pressed button under the pointer loses its accent background. Fixed for the zone toggle only.
- **Stale "today" in lists.** Lists read dates against the day they were first rendered, so a list left open across midnight keeps the old day.
- **No cross-tab sync.** The zone preference is not synced between open tabs; a reload picks it up.
- **Full suites not run.** They are left to the orchestrator, as instructed.

findings.summary: A failed header Refresh is now silent. The refresh token moved into the background token, so a rejected Refresh keeps the old data and never produces an error state. ErrorPanel and the "Loading failed." announcement never appear. On a finished run, and on the project and feature list pages, which have no live chip, nothing shows at all.
findings.failure_scenario:
1. Open a succeeded run, or /projects/

/workflows/. 2. Stop the API, or have /api/projects/... return a network error. 3. Press Refresh. The button shows "Refreshing…" and then "Refresh" again, and the page looks freshly loaded. - In the error branch, `same.value.status === 'ready'` keeps the value, sets `refresh: refreshToken` and failures to 1. `meta.refreshing` goes false, and state stays 'ready', so the announcer's message is unchanged. - On a succeeded or cancelled run, freshnessState returns 'finished' before it checks failures, and no polls follow. The chip says "Finished · not polling" forever. - Before S1, base contained refreshToken, so the same click gave the ErrorPanel ("could not be loaded") and announced "Loading failed." This brings back the "failed load keeps stale data with no warning" problem that PRD section 1 cites, now for an explicit user action. The handoff states "A failed Refresh keeps the shown data" without flagging it.

findings.summary: The run page no longer shows the run's date anywhere. Every run-page time is read against summary.created_at (TimeReferenceContext), so the Created fact is compared with itself and always renders as a bare clock. Updated and all other times show a date only if they fall on another day than the start. A run from yesterday or from months ago looks like it ran today; the date is only in a hover tooltip, which touch devices never show.
findings.failure_scenario:
View workflow-guardrails-001 (created 2026-09-23T19:32:52Z) on 2026-09-24:
- Created shows "19:32" (or "01:02" in Asia/Kolkata) and Updated shows "20:27". Nothing says Sep 23 or yesterday.
- Reproduced with formatClock(created, {zone, reference: created, now}), which returns '19:32'. A run created on 2026-03-01 and viewed in September gives '10:00'.
- ux-time.spec.ts:35 enshrines this: it expects Created of the March 1 fixture run to read '02:00'.
- Before S1 the page read "2026-09-23 19:32:52 UTC". "Since when?" is one of the PRD's five first-screen questions.

A fix: read the run's own start (or the whole run page when the run did not start today) against today, so the anchor gets "yesterday" or "Sep 23".

findings.summary: A Refresh no longer announces anything, and the now-disabled Refresh button drops keyboard focus to <body>. The announcer comment still promises "a load the reader started (navigation, Refresh) always announces". Because Refresh never passes through 'loading' any more, the message stays unchanged and the effect returns early at line 95.
findings.failure_scenario:
A keyboard or screen-reader user on a run page presses Enter on Refresh:
- The button becomes disabled (App.tsx:639). Chromium moves focus to BODY; I checked this with a minimal page, where the active element was BODY both during and after the disabled phase.
- When the reload completes, the announcer computes the same "Loaded run X: failed." message, and `message === announced.current` returns early. The user hears nothing and has lost their place.
- Before S1, the list blanked to loading, which reset `announced.current`, so the completed load was announced. The skills Refresh, which S1 copies, does announce "Refreshed …".

findings.summary: List times read dates against a "today" frozen by a useState initializer. It never updates on re-render or poll, only on remount. Because the workflow run list polls every 5 s, a list left open across midnight labels days wrongly indefinitely. The handoff's open issue says "until it re-renders", which is inaccurate.
findings.failure_scenario:
1. Open a feature's run list at 23:30.
2. A running run's updated_at advances to 00:05 the next day. The poll re-renders the same Time instance (same run_id key), which still holds yesterday's today.

It shows "Sep 25 00:05" for a time that is today; formatClock gives 'Sep 25 00:05' with the frozen `now`. A run updated at 23:50 keeps showing "23:50" instead of "yesterday 23:50".

findings.summary: The new Local/UTC toggle uses .button-small (min-height 30px), which is below the 44 px tap target that PRD section 10 requires at ≤760 px. No mobile rule enlarges it.
findings.failure_scenario: At a 390×844 viewport, the Local and UTC buttons are about 30 px tall. App.css:252 sets `.button-small { min-height: 30px }`, and the ≤760 px media block (App.css:429) does not override it. This fails the "Tap targets are at least 44 px" rule for a control S1 introduced.

spec_gaps: 12.3 migration: the `worker-stop` text should become "Stopped 10:20 · stop confirmed". It still reads "Stop confirmed at 10:20." (declared deviation 1). The reason is that lanes.spec.ts:102 pins "Stop confirmed", and 12.3 does not list that line. The PRD needs to either list lanes.spec.ts:102 under S1 or S4b, or accept the current wording.

12.2 time-local-utc should assert "A check row shows `3s`". It asserts 1m00s and 5m00s on existing checks instead. No 3 s check fixture was added to fixtures/ux-time.ts, although that module exists for exactly this. The sub-minute `Ns` format is covered only by the unit test.
Sections 11 and 12.2 say scenario ids go in `features/viewer-ux-<slice>/policy.json`. No policy registers time-local-utc and live-freshness (declared deviation 10, since S1 ships as a direct commit).
Section 10 requires 44 px tap targets at ≤760 px. The new time-zone-toggle buttons are 30 px tall (see findings).

Section 5.3 prefixes the date "only when it differs from the run's start day or today". As implemented, the run's own start is never dated on the run page (see findings). The PRD should say which reading is meant.
review.notes:

impl.deviations:
The full list with reasons is in `docs/handoff/ux-s2.md`.

**API shape**
1. `buildTimeline` takes `{detail, events, inputs?, review?, results?}` (results keyed by URI) and no `now`. Live spans have `end: null` and `live: true`, so the memoized timeline never goes stale every second.
2. The memo key is a superset of the PRD's (it adds node states, the event count and the results map).
3. A `controller_blocked` marker kind is added; 5.2 rule 5 names it but 5.1's list omits it. A "failed identically" row is one `diagnosis` marker with `blocked: true`.
4. `Timeline.activity` (Activity rows) and `lastActivity` are additions beyond 5.1's shape.
5. Headlines are rich-text parts (`clock`, `ago`, `span`, `elapsed`, `left`), so the approval's "(12 min)" renders as "12 min ago" and "working 5m" as "5m00s" with the default formatter.

**Controller rows**
6. A "Could not confirm worker stop" failure the controller recovered from is a `controller_error` marker, not a handoff failure (guardrails #7/#10/#13/#16).
7. B1's controller-row rule for a lane named `controller` is applied in the client until B1 lands.

**Timeline values**
8. No gap row is emitted while a non-worker step runs. The worker gap is 28m18s; the PRD's 28m21s is the worker's span.
9. Durations round to the nearest second: challenge attempt 2 shows 47s (PRD 46s), and the guardrails run span is 54m20s by rule 10 (PRD 4.1 says 54m21s, which counts the trailing PID row).
10. Focus ties are read as nodes in the same graph column; the latest event wins.

**Situation rules**
11. Rule 1 counts a question only while the run is not finished and the lane is not stopped.
12. Rule 3 adds `review "$RUN" --review-file <review.json>` for a manual review gate, and gives the manual handoff one `freeze` command with a `--handoff` flag per lane.
13. Rule 5(d) also matches a paused candidate after a candidate repair, reading "Continue with" from the `verify_<lane>` repair note.
14. Rule 7's step 4 is a copyable command.
15. Rule 8 on an automatic run requires the run to be `running`.
16. Reviewer panes use `--node review` or `--node review-<id>`.

**Scope**
17. Extra exports: `nowResultUris`, `controllerNotRunning`, `textToString`, `plainTextFormat` and constants.
18. Size: `triage.ts` is about 1,437 lines against the PRD's estimate of about 400, mostly the 13 situation builders, the Activity rows and doc comments.
19. Three results missing from the capture are derived in the test, as described in the summary.
impl.open_issues:
**S3**
- Fetch `nowResultUris(detail)` before trusting the banner, and treat a non-empty `Now.missing` as loading. Without `candidate_ui/1`, guardrails reads `no_rule_matched` with that URI in `missing`.
- Render `Text` parts with S1's `Time`, `formatSpan` and `formatAgo`, or pass a `TextFormat`.
- Hide `controller_log` rows behind "Controller log (n)".

**S5**
- Use `deriveFocus` and `humanizeEvent` for B2's `focus` and `headline`.
- Keep S5's `activity` type assignable to `ServedActivity` (`waiting_questions`, `attention`).
- The client already reads B1's statuses on node-less rows and the `[lane] ` candidate prefix.

**Known limit (C6)**
- Before B1, blocked rows belonging to a lane named `controller` (e.g. "Worker controller deadline exhausted") land on `launch_controller`. Rule 6 cannot quote them, so the run falls to rule 13 and shows the message as reason source 4.

**S1**
- S1's `test:unit` glob will collect `tests/unit/triage.test.ts`. Until it lands, run `npx tsx --test tests/unit/triage.test.ts`.

findings.summary: Rule 8 (check_failed) can never match an automatic run. It requires run status `running` together with a failed focus, but `projectSnapshot` serves the run as `failed` whenever any node is failed (`if (statuses.has('failed')) status = 'failed'`). A verify task keeps its graph error until the retry finishes, because `retry_check` clears nothing and `advance()` re-exports only after a step completes. So every automatic retry falls to rule 13.
findings.failure_scenario: skeleton-001 between #14 (09:20:20, attempt 1 failed) and #17 (09:21:30): the server serves verify_game failed (attempt 2 from the event), and the run failed, while the supervisor is retrying (#15 PID, #16 'Attempt 2' running). Reproduced with the served state: deriveNow gives situation `no_rule_matched`, headline '✗ Failed at Verify game · attempt 2 started · revision 5c1a734. The workflow did not complete.', next 'No known next step matched' plus `status "$RUN"`, and missing=[results/game/2]. That URI 404s until the attempt ends, so S3's 'treat missing as loading' holds for the whole retry. The same happens for candidate retries (guardrails #28 to #31, over 2 minutes). The PRD wanted 'No action: the supervisor retries by itself'. The unit test passes only because it builds an impossible snapshot (run `running` with verify_game `failed`). The cause is handoff deviation 15.

findings.summary: Rule 5(a) keeps saying 'Interrupted' after the operator resumes the run. The 'no later status event' test skips marker rows, so the resumed controller's PID row (a `controller_start` marker, served `running` with B1) never ends the interruption. The resumed `wait_handoffs` writes no other event until the worker changes state.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker is running when Ctrl-C writes 'Supervisor interrupted … resume with …'. The operator runs `automatic --live`, and a new 'Automatic checkpoint controller PID n' row follows. The server now serves handoff `pending` (the PID row is lastController), launch_game `running` and the run `running`. Reproduced both before B1 (PID status null) and with B1 (PID status running): deriveNow still gives `interrupted` case a: '‖ Interrupted at Launch game worker · 10:30: the controller stopped; sessions keep running', with `"$PY" -m workflow automatic "$RUN" --live` as a required step. Running that command fails with 'Another controller owns this run' (run_lock), and the wrong banner stays for the rest of the worker phase, which can be hours.

findings.summary: Rule 7's fallback, used when there is no diagnosis, treats two attempts as identical when their `error.message` values are equal, even across a repair. The controller also requires `same_revision(previous, path)`, and the budget restarts at the repair floor. `WorkerResult.output_commit` is available to compare, and `attemptFloor` already exists.
findings.failure_scenario: Attempts 1 and 2 fail identically, the operator applies repair 1 (new revision 50b14b3), and attempt 3 fails with the same reasons. Reproduced: deriveNow gives `blocked_identical`, headline '✗ Blocked at Verify game · lane game failed identically on attempts 2 and 3', and the five repair steps again. The controller does not consider this identical: it is attempt 1 of 3 on the new revision. An automatic run retries by itself, so the banner is wrong for the whole of attempt 4. A manual run should get rule 8's `retry --phase worker --node game`.

findings.summary: Rule 5(b) requires the focus to be `paused` and the run to be paused or running. The freeze note (FREEZE_RESUME_NOTE) and the Claude-unavailable review notes (automatic.py:624, :811) are written only on paths where the handoff or review task keeps its graph error. `freeze_failure()` and `review_interrupted()` both depend on that error, and `projectSnapshot` ranks `task.error` above the `interrupted`→`paused` event mapping. So the server serves those nodes, and the run, as `failed`. Only the Ctrl-C review case (automatic.py:804) is served paused. This is a wrong premise in PRD 6.2 5(b), followed literally.
findings.failure_scenario: Claude Code becomes unavailable during the freeze. The handoff gets 'Claude Code unavailable for 60s (…). The freeze was stopping the workers … resume with: python -m workflow automatic <path> --live', and the served state is handoff failed, run failed. Reproduced: `no_rule_matched`, '✗ Failed at Freeze worker handoffs · …', 'No known next step matched' plus `status`. The review variant gives '✗ Failed at Independent review · …' in the same way. This is exactly the output the PRD revision set out to remove. The 12.1 freeze test passes only because it builds handoff `paused` and run `paused`.

findings.summary: buildTimeline marks an in-progress retry attempt as `failed` with no end. `span.live` requires the node to be served running, and a span with no end on a non-live node takes the node status. During a retry the node is served `failed` (see the rule 8 finding), even though the attempt's 'Attempt k' running row is the node's latest status row.
findings.failure_scenario: Same served state as the rule 8 finding: verify_game failed at attempt 2, with events #1 running, #2 failed, a PID row and #4 'Attempt 2' running. Reproduced: byNode verify_game is [[1,'failed',end,false],[2,'failed',null,false]]. The Steps row and attempt markers would show attempt 2 as ✗ while it is still running, and its bar would not grow.

findings.summary: The handoff's 'Known limit (C6)' gives the wrong fallback. Before B1, a blocked row on a lane named `controller` falls to rule 13 with no reason at all, not with 'the message as reason source 4'. Rule 13's source 4 is the focus (handoff) node's last status message, and the handoff's only row after a block is the node-less `freeze stopped` record. B1 does not move 'Worker controller deadline exhausted' off the lane either, because it matches none of the controller-process patterns, so the limit outlives B1.
findings.failure_scenario: A two-lane run with lanes `controller` and `ui` hits a deadline before freeze. The events are the raw `controller blocked 'Worker ui deadline exhausted…'` (aliased onto launch_controller) and then `freeze stopped` 'Native workers stopped…'. The served state is launches succeeded, handoff failed, run failed. Reproduced: '✗ Failed at Freeze worker handoffs · no reason was recorded.' The deadline cause is lost. S3 and S5 are told a different behaviour.

findings.summary: Rule 5(c) sets `since` to the first `not_running` reading in the whole history, not the start of the current not-running streak that `controllerNotRunning` measured.
findings.failure_scenario: Readings are a hand-over blip at 10:00:10 (not_running), running at 10:00:15, then not_running at 10:50:00 and 10:50:20. Reproduced: `interrupted` case c with `since` 10:00:10, where 10:50:00 is expected. S3 would show 'since' 50 minutes too early.

spec_gaps: 12.1 `check_failed` requires 'Automatic: no command'. That is tested only on a snapshot the server never serves (run `running` with verify `failed`). With the real served state (run `failed`), the automatic case produces `no_rule_matched`, so the 12.1 row is not met.

12.1 `interrupted` (b) freeze (and the Claude-unavailable review variant) is tested only with the node served `paused`. FREEZE_RESUME_NOTE is written only when the handoff task keeps its error, which the server serves as `failed`, so the case never matches real payloads. PRD 6.2 5(b)'s premise ('the server maps the raw interrupted status to paused on that node') needs correcting together with the rule.

6.2 rule 5(a) as the PRD specifies it ('no later status event') does not say that the resumed controller's PID row ends the interruption. With B1 the PID row is served `status: running`, which should count. The implementation excludes it (see finding).

6.2 rule 7's 'latest two attempt results have the same error.message' fallback omits the controller's same-revision condition (automatic.py advance_failed_checks). Without it, rule 7 misfires after a repair (see finding).

Minor quality points, not listed as findings:
- `Internal.lastActivityText` duplicates `Timeline.lastActivity.note`.
- `laneOf` slices 'launch_'.length for 'verify_' too; it works only because both prefixes are 7 characters.
- The memo compares `results` by identity, so S3 must pass a new Map when it adds results rather than mutating one (this is documented).

The two P1s share a root cause: the triage assumes node and run statuses the server does not serve during retries and resumes. A fix should read the event log instead: an 'Attempt k' running row after the last failure means a live retry, and a PID row (or B2 `controller: running`) after an interrupted row means the run was resumed.

outcomes.item: P1 contracts/projects/triage.ts:1217 — rule 8 (check_failed) never matches an automatic run because the run is served failed during a retry
outcomes.note: Confirmed: projectSnapshot ranks task.error first and fails the run with any failed node, and retry_check clears nothing. New retryPlan(): a failed verify or candidate below its cap on the lane's revision, not identical, with no in-scope controller block. It matches whatever the run status is. While a retry runs (verdictAttempt/reentered), the failed attempt's result is read, the headline adds '· attempt k running since HH:MM', and the running attempt's URI is never put in missing. Tests use skeleton-001 as served at #14 and #16 and guardrails at #30. A block row after the failure falls to rule 13 as source 0. Handoff deviation 15 is rewritten.

outcomes.item: P1 contracts/projects/triage.ts:1078 — rule 5(a) keeps saying Interrupted after the operator resumes (the PID row is ignored)
outcomes.note: (a) now also ends at a later controller_start marker or a controller block, not only at a later status row. Tested with the PID row status null (before B1) and 'running' (B1): it reads 'running' with only attach-one. The same defect existed in (b) (a resumed Ctrl-C review writes no row until its verdict), so a PID row after the note ends (b) too, and rule 10 shows '● Running · <step> · resumed at HH:MM'.

outcomes.item: P2 contracts/projects/triage.ts:1188 — rule 7 fallback treats attempts across a repair as identical
outcomes.note: identicalLanes() now requires sameRevision(output_commit), mirroring automatic.py same_revision (an unknown commit counts as the same). failingLanes reads the previous attempt only above the repair floor (attemptFloor). Tests: same revision gives blocked_identical, another revision gives check_failed, and across repair 1 gives check_failed 'attempt 1 of 3' (automatic, no command; manual gets retry --phase worker --node game).

outcomes.item: P2 contracts/projects/triage.ts:1090 — rule 5(b) requires a paused focus, but the freeze and outage review notes are served failed
outcomes.note: Confirmed for FREEZE_RESUME_NOTE (:1314) and the review outage notes (:624, :811), which keep task.error; only the Ctrl-C note (:804) is served paused. interruptionNote() reads the note from the focus's latest row (the row itself is served paused) and accepts a focus served paused or failed. Rule 5's run-status gate now also admits failed runs, which also fixes the :1316 UNAVAILABLE_NOTE case for (a). Tests cover the review outage served failed, the freeze served failed, and a resumed freeze reading running.

outcomes.item: P2 contracts/projects/triage.ts:576 — buildTimeline marks an in-progress retry as failed with no end
outcomes.note: An open span of a node served failed is live when its row is the node's latest status row. In automatic runs no PID row may follow it (automatic-step exits only once its step ended); in manual runs it must be a retry. skeleton #16 now gives verify_game [[1,failed,end,false],[2,running,null,true]], and a later PID row ends it. laneLines shows it as ● (guardrails as served at #25).

outcomes.item: P3 docs/handoff/ux-s2.md:170 — 'Known limit (C6)' describes the wrong fallback
outcomes.note: The handoff is corrected: the first round printed 'no reason was recorded', and B1 does not move 'Worker <lane> deadline exhausted' off launch_controller. The model now also keeps the cause: rule 13's source 4 falls back to the failed dependency row that opened the scope window when the focus has no row. Test: a two-lane run with a lane named controller gives '✗ Failed at Freeze worker handoffs · Worker ui deadline exhausted; no automatic relaunch.' with reasonSource 4.

outcomes.item: P3 contracts/projects/triage.ts:1103 — rule 5(c) since uses the first not_running reading in history
outcomes.note: New notRunningSince() returns the start of the current not_running streak. controllerNotRunning uses it, and so does (c). Tested with the reviewer's readings: since is 10:50:00.

outcomes.item: gap — 12.1 check_failed 'Automatic: no command' tested only on an impossible snapshot
outcomes.note: The check_failed tests now use the real served states (run failed): skeleton-001 at #14 and #16, and the guardrails candidate at #30. All give check_failed with no command. The proposed 12.1 wording is in the handoff (the PRD is outside S2's files).

outcomes.item: gap — 12.1 interrupted (b) freeze and review-outage cases tested only with the node served paused; the PRD 6.2 5(b) premise is wrong
outcomes.note: The rule and the tests use the served states (node and run failed); the Ctrl-C review stays paused. The handoff lists the PRD 6.2 5(b) premise correction as proposed and not applied, because the PRD is outside S2's file list.

outcomes.item: gap — 6.2 rule 5(a) 'no later status event' does not say the resumed PID row ends it
outcomes.note: Implemented: a PID row or a controller block after the row ends (a), and a PID row ends (b). Handoff deviation 19 and the proposed PRD wording are recorded.

outcomes.item: gap — 6.2 rule 7 fallback omits the controller's same_revision condition
outcomes.note: Implemented (same output_commit, previous attempt above the repair floor). Handoff deviation 22 and the proposed PRD wording are recorded.
